lesson.title: Stomach position, relations and neurovascular supply
lesson.summary: Follow the curves before memorizing arteries.

lesson.section: 14. Stomach: Position, Parts, and Relations; 15. Stomach Blood Supply, Lymphatics, and Innervation

steps.title: Stomach: Position, Parts, and Relations
steps.body:
The stomach is an intraperitoneal foregut organ in the epigastric and left hypochondriac regions. It has cardia, fundus, body, pyloric antrum, pyloric canal, and pylorus, with lesser and greater curvatures.

Anterior relations include diaphragm, left lobe of liver, and anterior abdominal wall. Posterior relations form the stomach bed: diaphragm, spleen, left kidney, left suprarenal gland, pancreas, transverse mesocolon, and colon. The lesser curvature gives attachment to lesser omentum; greater curvature gives attachment to greater omentum and gastrosplenic ligament. The pylorus is commonly near the transpyloric plane in the supine position.

steps.title: Stomach Blood Supply, Lymphatics, and Innervation
steps.body:
The stomach is supplied by branches of the celiac trunk. Arteries run mainly along the lesser and greater curvatures and send branches onto the anterior and posterior gastric walls.

Left and right gastric arteries run along the lesser curvature. Left and right gastro-omental arteries run along the greater curvature. Short gastric arteries supply the fundus. Venous drainage follows arteries to the portal venous system. Parasympathetic supply is from anterior and posterior vagal trunks; sympathetic supply comes through celiac plexus.

steps.title: How does stomach rotation help explain vagal trunk orientation?
steps.body: During development the stomach's left surface becomes predominantly anterior and its right surface predominantly posterior. The left vagus consequently contributes mainly to the anterior vagal trunk and the right mainly to the posterior trunk. Plexus mixing means the adult trunks are not perfectly isolated left and right cables. This developmental account connects nerve position with peritoneal and curvature changes. It also illustrates why anterior in an adult diagram need not correspond to anterior in the earliest embryonic tube.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: Follow the curves before memorizing arteries. The lesser curvature receives gastric arteries, the greater curvature gastro-omental arteries, and the fundus short gastric branches. The lesser sac separates much of the posterior stomach from the pancreas and other stomach-bed relations. Posterior gastric disease can therefore affect adjacent structures through these relations. Vagal trunks bring parasympathetic fibers; visceral pain pathways are a different functional component of the gastric plexuses.
